text:
Tottenham make January decision regarding 29-year-old Bundesliga target

Tottenham have reportedly decided not to make a new centre-back their priority in the January transfer window, despite their difficult start to the season.

The north London club have endured a difficult campaign so far, with their defensive performances raising questions about whether they’ll need another addition when the transfer window reopens.

Tottenham trust their current defensive options

However, according to Football Insider, Tottenham are not currently planning to prioritise another centre-back after making significant investments in that area during the summer.

Roberto De Zerbi strengthened his defensive options with the arrivals of Jan-Paul van Hecke, Marcos Senesi and Tosin, adding depth to a department that had already been reshaped.

Despite Tottenham conceding three goals in three separate matches this season, the club’s recruitment plans are not expected to change significantly in January. De Zerbi reportedly remains satisfied with the options available to him and does not view another central defender as an immediate necessity.

Want more CaughtOffside coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

Kim Min-jae could have been useful

One name linked with Tottenham is Bayern Munich defender Kim Min-jae, but the report claims the 29-year-old South Korean is unlikely to move to north London during the upcoming window.

Tottenham have admired the experienced defender before, but their recent spending means another major investment in the position is not currently seen as essential.

Micky van de Ven and Van Hecke have emerged as De Zerbi’s preferred partnership at the back, while Senesi and Tosin provide additional competition for places.

There is also reportedly no intention to let Van de Ven leave, despite interest from Liverpool and Manchester United. The Dutch international recently signed a new contract and remains an important part of Tottenham’s plans.

With the club looking to recover from a disappointing opening to the campaign, their January recruitment strategy could therefore focus on other areas rather than another centre-back.

text:
“Great signing” – Chelsea praised for smart transfer business that’s already paying off

Chelsea have been praised for the summer signing of Danny Welbeck, who has shone since his surprise move from Brighton.

The 35-year-old has had a long and successful career in the Premier League, though he’s arguably shown his best form in the last few years.

Welbeck started out as a youngster at Manchester United, but he struggled for regular first-team football there before moving to Arsenal in 2014.

After five years at Arsenal, Welbeck moved to Watford and then to Brighton a year later, with the former England international going on to score 51 goals in 201 appearances.

Although he’s only likely to be a squad player for Chelsea, Welbeck has started brightly at Stamford Bridge, with three goals in three games so far.

Former Chelsea star praises Danny Welbeck signing

Former Chelsea striker Jimmy-Floyd Hasselbaink is a big fan of Welbeck, praising his old club for this signing due to the qualities the veteran forward can bring both on and off the pitch.

“But he can give so much to the other players on and off the pitch. He will be talking to the other players and helping that way but also he wants to score and he will want to be on the end of things.

“It’s a great signing for Chelsea.”

Chelsea’s current ownership were going a little overboard with their focus on signing young players, so they deserve some credit for recruiting experienced players like Welbeck and Jordan Henderson this summer.

name: prod 32: MLS’s transfer window and the spending line that keeps going up
text:
MLS’s transfer window and the spending line that keeps going up

Summer spending across the league’s 30 clubs has ballooned. Here are three takeaways from the league’s transfer window

With the shadow of the 2026 World Cup hanging over the league and a potential set of rule changes looming, Major League Soccer’s summer transfer window was one defined by uncertainty, diverse strategies and record spending. It was the fourth transfer window since MLS allowed clubs to purchase players from other clubs using traditional transfer fees rather than general allocation money (GAM), the intraleague currency system. The new rule, which is now being used more frequently, has helped account for rapid growth in league expenditure, as has increased GAM allotted to each club.

These trends have been seen broadly over the last two seasons, but this past window took it to a new level, smashing the previous record for summer spending. This summer, MLS teams spent 65% more year-over-year, with a total of nearly $190m spent, accounting for 45% of the 2026 total. The above factors combined to create one of the most consequential transfer windows in MLS history, which may give a glimpse into the league’s future trajectory.

name: prod 46: Tottenham make major Micky van de Ven decision amid Liverpool transfer
text:
Tottenham make major Micky van de Ven decision amid Liverpool transfer interest

Tottenham have no intention of selling Micky van de Ven amid continued speculation linking the defender with a future move to Liverpool.

The Netherlands international has been mentioned as a potential long-term successor to Virgil van Dijk at Anfield, but Spurs are reportedly relaxed about the situation.

Van de Ven only signed a new contract until 2031 in August and has since been made Tottenham captain, leaving the North London club in a strong position over his future.

Tottenham ‘won’t entertain’ Micky van de Ven sale

Speaking on Football Insider’s Transfer Insider podcast, Pete O’Rourke explained why Tottenham are not concerned by the interest surrounding the 25-year-old.

“Tottenham are quite relaxed about this. They tied down Van de Ven to a new contract in August until 2031.

“So look, Tottenham hold all the aces here, he’s been made club captain as well, so I can’t imagine they’ll be too keen to lose such a key player.”

O’Rourke went on to deliver an emphatic update regarding the possibility of Tottenham sanctioning a transfer.

“Tottenham won’t be entertaining a sale anytime soon. Top players will always attract interest and have suitors, but he’s under a long-term contract at Tottenham and they’re planning for life with Micky van de Ven.”

The length of Van de Ven’s contract means there is little immediate pressure on Spurs to consider offers, while handing him the captaincy further underlines his importance to the club.

Liverpool have been linked with Micky van de Ven

It has previously been reported that Liverpool have identified Van de Ven as a potential candidate to eventually succeed Van Dijk at the heart of their defence.

It is easy to understand why the Dutchman would appeal to Liverpool.

Van de Ven possesses exceptional recovery pace alongside his physical strength and ability on the ball, while he already has extensive Premier League experience.

However, Tottenham’s position means any potential pursuit would be extremely difficult.

With Van de Ven contracted until 2031 and established as club captain, Spurs have little incentive to negotiate over one of their most important players.

Jeremy Jacquet emerging as Liverpool’s Van Dijk successor

Liverpool may also already have a potential long-term Van Dijk successor at Anfield in Jeremy Jacquet.

The young French defender has produced a series of impressive performances since arriving on Merseyside and has already shown encouraging signs alongside Van Dijk.

Jacquet’s recent displays have further strengthened his reputation, including an excellent performance on his full senior debut for France during the international break.

That could reduce the urgency for Liverpool to spend heavily on another centre-back.

Van de Ven’s profile understandably makes him an attractive option, but Tottenham’s refusal to contemplate a sale and Jacquet’s rapid development mean Liverpool may already have a more straightforward solution to their long-term defensive succession plan.

Alexis Mac Allister makes his point as Liverpool fight back to defeat Atlético

It was the time and place for Alexis Mac Allister to do his talking on the pitch and the disgruntled Liverpool midfielder delivered on cue. “Very sad” over Liverpool’s refusal to offer him a new contract, while Dominik Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch were getting theirs, Mac Allister made Anfield very happy with a match-winning display against Atlético Madrid.

The Argentina international, one of five World Cup finalists involved in an absorbing, delicately-poised contest, vented his frustrations in the best possible and most professional way – from behind an immaculate 20-yard strike into Jan Oblak’s goal rather than a microphone. Mac Allister believes he is playing for a new deal this season and promised to give “100% to my last day” at the pre-match press conference. He was true to his word to extend Atlético’s winless sequence against English opposition in the Champions League league phase to 11 matches.

name: prod 66: Thomas Tuchel makes huge Harry Kane claim after England’s stunning 7-0
text:
Thomas Tuchel makes huge Harry Kane claim after England’s stunning 7-0 win

England thrashed Croatia 7-0 to claim their second win out of three in the UEFA Nations League group stages.

Thomas Tuchel’s side produced a scintillating tactical masterclass at the Stadion Rujevica in Rijeka, storming into a commanding 4-0 lead before the break and refusing to take their foot off the gas in the second half.

Harry Kane and Bukayo Saka shine as England destroy Croatia

The attacking duo of Harry Kane and Bukayo Saka stole the show as both star forwards bagged clinical double strikes during the historic away triumph.

Kane opened the scoring in the eighth minute after latching onto a slick pass from Jude Bellingham, firing high into the roof of the net.

Bellingham doubled the advantage shortly after before Anthony Gordon nodded in a third.

Saka grabbed his first right before half-time to cap off a rampant opening 45 minutes. Kane netted his second early in the second period, followed by Saka’s second, before substitute Morgan Rogers rounded off the magnificent seven late in the contest.

Seven goals. One unforgettable night for England ????????

The Three Lions ran riot against Croatia in a 7-0 Nations League demolition ?

Sit back and enjoy EVERY goal ???#Internationalfootball pic.twitter.com/Z3MtP20cdF

— DAZN Football (@DAZNFootball) October 3, 2026

Thomas Tuchel full of praise for Harry Kane

Following the statement victory, manager Thomas Tuchel praised skipper Harry Kane’s irreplaceable quality at the highest level of world football.

“Harry Kane is the highest level of striker possible. You will not get another Harry Kane,” Tuchel stated post-match.

“There will be someone else, but it will not be Harry or a copy of Harry. We will find a solution… but maybe not me. It might be another 10 years!”

text:
WSL talking points: Chelsea punish Arsenal and Putellas finds her rhythm

Gunners lacked cutting edge again at Stamford Bridge while the former Barcelona star dominated against Brighton

How to solve the problem of an inability to take your chances? That is the question that will haunt the Arsenal head coach, Renée Slegers, over the coming days. In their 1-0 defeat by Chelsea, Arsenal applied more than enough pressure to make a difference, but in registering two of their 18 shots on target, a fundamental lack of ruthlessness remains. They dominated the opening stages at Stamford Bridge, but, as has often been the case this season, they were made to pay for their wastefulness. None of their nine first-half attempts troubled the goalkeeper, Hannah Hampton. Chelsea, however, had five of eight on target and scored just before half-time through Alyssa Thompson. “I wanted to keep it away from the players because they can score goals and they can finish and they will get the rewards for their work,” Slegers said. Solutions need to be found quickly. Sophie Downey

name: prod 74: Premier League summer signing admits he would have joined Manchester U
text:
Premier League summer signing admits he would have joined Manchester United

Belgian defender Thomas Meunier joined Sunderland in the summer transfer window, and he has said he would have joined elite clubs like Manchester United if he had the choice.

The 34-year-old joined the Black Cats on a free transfer from a French outfit. In a recent interview, the defender said transfers are sometimes not up to the player, and he would have preferred to join clubs like Manchester United, Bayern Munich, or Real Madrid.

However, Sunderland’s pitch was convincing, and he had an impressive phone call with their manager, Regis Le Bris.

Thomas Meunier reveals Manchester United preference

“You don’t always get to choose exactly where you want to go,” he said (h/t Walfoot).

“Otherwise, I’d have gone to Bayern Munich, Real Madrid, or Manchester United! But seriously, they called me and were incredibly convincing.”

Meunier has been a quality player at the top level in recent years, and his experience could prove to be valuable for Sunderland. They did quite well after securing promotion to the Premier League last year, and they have qualified for European football this season.

They will look to build on it and sustain that level of performance in the coming months. They needed more quality and experience in the team. The 34-year-old defender should prove to be an excellent short-term investment on a free transfer.
